text:
maya: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert -> high 5xx rate from us-east-2b egress paths. Customer reports for Dedicated pools in us-east-2 show external API timeouts.
incident-bot: [INCIDENT OPENED] id=INC-2026-1855001234 severity=sev2 region=us-east-2 impact=egress
maya: Observing spike at 14:20 UTC, flows to external endpoints dropped, traceroutes show last hop in AZB NAT layer.
samir: I'm oncall, paging in. grabbing runbook_egress_nag (link) and joining bridge.
jules: seeing same in logs—connection resets and TLS handshakes failing on nat-gw-azb.
kevin: quick check: are route tables correct? ran `aws ec2 describe-route-tables --filters Name=association.subnet-id,Values=subnet-azb-*` and some subnets in AZB point to a target that looks stale.
lia: I pushed a tiny NACL egress deny change 10m ago for a security test on one subnet group. Rolling that back now.
lia: rolled back NACL change -> `aws ec2 replace-network-acl-entry --network-acl-id acl-0abcd --rule-number 100 --egress false --cidr-block 0.0.0.0/0 --port-range From=0,To=65535 --protocol -1 --rule-action allow`
maya: NACL rollback propagated, but errors still persist. Metrics improved slightly for some hosts but others still failing.
samir: hypothesis: NAT gateway in AZB ENI is flapping or its elastic IP lost route propagation. Can someone check NAT health and ENI status?
kevin: checked `describe-nat-gateways` - nat-0a1b2c3d shows state=available but has high `failed_association_count`. ENI for nat-0a1b2c3d shows frequent attachments/detachments in CloudTrail.
jules: I see cross-AZ route propagation jitter in the VPC route table. Some associations momentarily pointed to a blackhole target (com.amazonaws.vpce).
ops-bot: Automated failover suggestion: re-associate route table in AZB to nat-standby-azeast2 (other AZ NAT) or create temporary nat instance. Confirm to proceed?
samir: Proceed with safe failover to nat-standby-azeast2 for affected subnets. Keep canary subset first (2 subnets), then bulk.
maya: On it — applying route replace to two canary subnets now.
kevin: Command I ran for canary (logged):
```
aws ec2 replace-route --route-table-id rtb-azb-public-1 --destination-cidr-block 0.0.0.0/0 --gateway-id nat-standby-azeast2
```
lia: canary subnets traffic now flows through standby NAT and external checks pass for those hosts. :white_check_mark:
samir: Good. Start rolling remaining affected subnets in small batches, 30s between changes. Notify if any regressions.
jules: Rolling now, batch 1/4 complete.
maya: During batch 2 we saw an app that relies on source IP preservation break (SAML callback fails). That's expected when changing NAT. Temporarily pinned that app to dedicated egress path.
kevin: Also noticed DNS lateral failures — the DNS resolver in AZB occasionally returning SERVFAIL for external domains around the time of NAT flaps. Could be that recursive resolvers lost egress.
samir: Mitigation: we should move resolver traffic to the standby NAT too. Lia can update resolver route.
lia: Updating resolver subnet route to standby NAT... done. DNS checks passing for canary.
maya: Customer impact: ~15% of Dedicated customers in us-east-2 had transient external call failures for ~18 minutes, one customer reported failed webhooks and we opened a support ticket. No data plane loss for internal traffic.
incident-bot: Impact annotation: partial external egress failures for a subset of Dedicated pools in us-east-2; estimated affected customers=~12-20; ETA to full mitigation unknown.
samir: Next: figure root cause. Two leading suspects: (1) ENI flapping on nat-0a1b2c3d due to host HW or cloud provider route instability; (2) a bad NACL or recent automation change that caused asymmetric routing and broke some flows.
kevin: Pulling CloudTrail and VPCFlow logs around 14:05-14:30 UTC and correlating with NAT gateway metrics.
jules: I see a config change event at 14:07 UTC from infra-automation user that updated a route propagation tag on RTB-azb. Could be correlated.
maya: Paging cloud provider support (support-case #123456). Adding transcript and metrics.
ops-bot: Reminder: create incident channel #inc-azb-egress-1855001234 for coordination if we want persistent chat.
samir: Creating channel, moving long-running ops there. Also handover note: I'll be primary until 15:00 UTC then hand to Maya.
maya: I'll take postmortem lead and customer comms after mitigation. Please add any affected customer IDs to the incident doc.
kevin: After full failover and resolver routing, last checks show egress success rates back to normal for 90% of hosts, remaining flappers are being isolated.
lia: Found one subnet where a security automation re-applied a hardened NACL template at 14:06 UTC — that explains the partial regressions. I've disabled automation on the VPC and applied allow rules.
jules: Verified backend health; no host-level crashes, just network path issues.
maya: Notifying Support and Customer Success with impact summary and ticket numbers.
incident-bot: [INCIDENT UPDATE] severity remains sev2 -> possible sev1 if external partners escalate.
samir: We're going to continue monitoring for 30 minutes. If stable, we'll start a gradual rollback of the temporary NAT re-route back to normal architecture once NAT gateway is confirmed healthy or replacement NAT is provisioned.
maya: Adding quick runbook excerpt to chat: `If NAT gateway shows ENI flapping, fail traffic to standby AZ NAT and open provider case. If NACL automation applied undesired rules, disable automation and restore allow rules.`
kevin: Final note for now: Cloud provider reported an internal routing flap in us-east-2 affecting a subset of ENIs — they are tracking. We applied customer-impact mitigation (standby NAT re-route + NACL rollback).
maya: Closing temporary mitigation window. Will keep monitoring and will post a P0 timeline + RCA draft in 24h. Thanks all. :heart:
poi: reaction summary (not a real user): :thumbsup: 12 :coffee: 3 :rotating_light: 1
